subject: Intermittent uploads & high latency after VPN cutover - SNAT / MTU suspicion
messages:
From: Edward Jenkins <edward.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurora NetOps <netops@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:45:00-05:00
Subject: Uploads timing out & slow token responses after VPN cutover

Hi Priya,

We completed the VPN cutover to the Redwood Private gateway this morning (per the cutover runbook). Since then we're seeing: high upload latency for >1MB payloads to the inference endpoint, intermittent 504s on long-running requests, and a spike in SYN retransmits on our concentrators. Basic checks show a flurry of TCP MSS/fragmentation events. The issue is affecting a subset of gateways in us-east-1 only.

Attached is a short tcpdump from our aggregator showing SYN retries and ICMP fragmentation-needed messages. We've also included our post-cutover topology diagram. Can Redwood confirm whether you're seeing increased SNAT counts / conntrack churn on your edge?

This is impacting an active pilot — we'd like a quick triage and mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Edward
Edward Jenkins
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Aurora Health

Attachment: tcpdump-syn-retrans.pcap (pcap)
Attachment: aurora-topology-diagram.pdf (pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Edward Jenkins <edward.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Aurora NetOps <netops@aurorahealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T16:10:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Uploads timing out & slow token responses after VPN cutover

Edward — thanks for the packet capture and topology. I've looped in Kar thik and Marissa from Private Network Ops. Initial read: the ICMP "fragmentation needed" plus SYN retries smells like an MTU mismatch somewhere along the VPN <-> on-prem path, and SNAT port pressure could be exacerbating tail latency for long-lived flows.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- Kar thik will validate the MTU applied to the egress tunnel and check if we recently flipped an MSS clamp on the VPN.
- Marissa will pull per-POD conntrack and SNAT allocation graphs for the affected edge pool (us-east-1 / pool-a).
- We'll ask Aurora for an intermediate tcpdump on the spoke side (pre-VPN) showing the PMTU/ICMP flow.

Can you confirm whether the pilot traffic uses persistent keepalives from the same inside IPs (i.e., heavy reuse) or many short-lived connections? That will help prioritize conntrack tuning vs. MTU fix.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: Edward Jenkins <edward.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>, Aurora NetOps <netops@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T18:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Uploads timing out & slow token responses after VPN cutover

Folks — I've pulled the edge pool metrics for pool-a (us-east-1) and correlate the timestamps in Edward's capture:
- SNAT port exhaustion events spike at 15:30–15:40 UTC (aligned with cutover).
- conntrack table churn shows entries with TTLs being reaped quickly (lots of short-lived 1-3s flows).
- We have an MSS clamp change recorded in the gateway config at 2026-11-03T14:50:12 UTC pushed accidentally with a lower clamp (MSS 1200) during the cutover automation.

Immediate hypothesis: the MSS clamp reduced effective payload size causing more fragmentation-handling ICMPs; combined with many short-lived uploads this inflated ephemeral port usage and caused transient SNAT stall/queueing.

Actions I've kicked off (working with Infra team):
1) Revert MSS clamp to 1420 on the affected tunnels (will do at 18:15 UTC).
2) Increase conntrack hashsize and ephemeral port pool for the row of NAT boxes serving Aurora traffic — temporary bump for the next 48 hours.
3) Add a temporary application-level keepalive recommendation to Aurora to reuse sockets for uploads where possible.
4) Marissa, please surface any eBPF drops or sg-block logs that could contribute.

I'll post status after the revert attempt.

-Karthik
Senior Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Edward Jenkins <edward.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>, Aurora NetOps <netops@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:32:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Uploads timing out & slow token responses after VPN cutover

Update — reverted MSS clamp at 2026-11-03T18:17:05 UTC and increased conntrack sizes + ephemeral port allocation. Observations:
- Packet-level ICMP fragmentation-needed messages dropped dramatically after the revert.
- SNAT exhaustion counters are back to baseline but we did see a second smaller spike around 02:00 local time (likely a batch from Aurora).
- I also checked security groups — no denies seen for the relevant subnets (no SG policy hit).

Next ask for Aurora: please run one-minute tcpdump capturing the same upload flow from an on-prem spoke during a pilot run and share. If you can also provide a quick app-side trace showing whether uploads open new TCP connections for each file, that will confirm the short-lived flow hypothesis.

I'll keep the temporary conntrack/ephemeral port bump in place until Wednesday EOD. We should consider a longer-term mitigation: either increase NAT pool or move Aurora into a reserved NAT cluster with higher port space and sticky NAT for long-lived sessions.

— Marissa
Network Ops Lead, Redwood Private

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Edward Jenkins <edward.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, netops@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Uploads timing out & slow token responses after VPN cutover — next steps and playbook

Edward — quick summary and plan so we have an operational playbook for you and our teams:
1) Root cause: accidental MSS clamp change during cutover caused PMTU issues; coupled with many short-lived upload connections this led to ephemeral port pressure and transient SNAT queuing.
2) Short-term mitigation already applied: MSS clamp revert, conntrack/ephemeral port temporary increase, and monitoring. We saw immediate improvement.
3) Recommended actions for Aurora (to finalize this week):
   - Configure your upload client to reuse TCP connections where possible (HTTP keepalive).
   - If stickiness is acceptable, allow Redwood to provision a reserved NAT cluster for Aurora with sticky SNAT and larger port space (we can provide sizing).
   - Run a controlled test with a 2MB and 8MB payload from a spoke and share tcpdumps for confirmation.
4) Redwood follow-ups:
   - Marissa will collect eBPF traces around the 02:00 spiky batch and propose a threshold-based autoscale for NAT pool.
   - Karthik will document the MSS/clamp guardrail and add it to the cutover checklist to prevent future accidental changes.
   - We'll keep the temporary NAT tuning for 48 hours and then schedule a short maintenance window for a non-disruptive long-term NAT remap if Aurora opts in.

Do you want us to open a dedicated maintenance window this week to run the reserved NAT allocation test? If so, suggest two 1-hour slots (UTC).

Thanks for the quick help and patience — glad this returned to baseline after the revert.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
